text:
maria: Quick heads-up — starting implementation plan for AWS KMS in Redwood Private (control-plane + data-plane). Need to align on envelope flows, rotation automation, cross-account grants, and emergency failover. TL;DR questions below.

jon: +1. For envelope: control-plane will hold CMK access and will rewrap DEKs; data-plane only sees encrypted DEKs and the runtime caches DEKs per-GPU node, yes?

maria: Yes. Design: customer CMK (or Redwood-managed CMK) in customer account for control-plane; control-plane uses kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:ReEncrypt to manage DEKs. Data-plane nodes get encrypted DEKs and only request rewraps when cache misses or rotation.

aditya: Question: DEK caching TTL vs rotation. If we rotate CMK daily, how do we ensure DEKs are rewrapped without causing spike/latency on warm nodes? Thoughts: stagger rewrap, background rewrap for hot keys.

jon: Stagger + push-based rewrap. When rotation happens, mark DEK metadata as needing rewrap; nodes continue with cached plaintext DEK until expiry (short TTL e.g. 10m) then lazy rewrap on next request. Also run a background job to proactively rewrap cold DEKs to avoid thundering herd.

tess: Cross-account CMKs: we'll grant our control-plane role a Grant to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:ReEncrypt. Avoid long-lived grants — create grants with constraints (EncryptionContext keys) and rotate grants when roles change. Example grant usage snippet in policy: 
```json
{"Sid":"ControlPlaneGrant","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane"},"Action":["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:ReEncryptFrom","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"*"}
```
(we'll use proper ARNs and conditions in practice)

sec-bot: Note: Audit logging requires CloudTrail for KMS events and CloudWatch/GuardDuty alerts on ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey. Also enable key usage logging: CloudTrail -> send to central log account.

ops: VPC note: use AWS KMS interface VPC endpoint (com.amazonaws.<region>.kms) for Private deployments to ensure KMS traffic stays in the VPC. Also whitelist KMS endpoint in our egress policies.

maria: Command examples for ops/setup: 
```bash
# create alias for control-plane CMK
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/redwood_private_controlplane --target-key-id abcdef12-3456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 --region us-west-2

# re-encrypt DEK in-place (rehydrate encrypted blob)
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted-dek.bin --destination-key-id alias/redwood_private_controlplane --region us-west-2 --output text > rewrapped-dek.bin
```

aditya: Rewrap automation: propose Lambda triggered by Key Rotation event or a scheduled job that: list DEK objects needing rewrap (from metadata DB), call ReEncrypt, update DB atomically. Add rate limiter to avoid KMS quota bursts.

jon: Important: KMS quotas and throttling — limit concurrent ReEncrypt calls per-account and add exponential backoff on 5xx/Throttling. We should instrument per-rotation-run metrics so SRE can tune concurrency.

sre-bot: Incident playbook idea: if KMS becomes unavailable/slow:
- flip to degraded control-plane mode: disallow new writes that require immediate GenerateDataKey; allow read/serve using cached DEKs (respecting TTL)
- surface alerts and an incident runbook to re-enable writes after KMS recovery + verification
- avoid fallback to plaintext keys; only allow emergency offline key escrow (requires manual approval and audit)

maria: Agree — we must avoid automated plaintext fallback. For disaster recovery, documented manual procedure with OPA/2-person approval and an auditable rollback.

tess: One more: rotation and rewrap safety — add an "original_key_id" field in DEK metadata so we can re-encrypt back if needed. Also store encryption context checksum so ReEncrypt requests have context validation.

ops: On audit retention: centralize CloudTrail logs for KMS to our security account and keep at least 1 year WORM for customers requesting compliance. Tag logs with customer id and key alias.

aditya: Edge-case: what if a customer rotates their CMK outside our flow (they call KMS RotateKey or create/disable)? We should detect CMK changes (via CloudTrail or DescribeKey webhook) and enqueue rewraps, but also surface to customer with a best-effort ETA for completion.

jon: Agreed. Also add a pre-rotation validation step in our docs: recommend customers schedule rotations through our control-plane or notify us a maintenance window.

sec-bot: Quick checklist to implement this week: enable CloudTrail for KMS -> central account, create control-plane IAM role + least-privilege policy, configure VPC endpoint, implement rewrap lambda + rate limiter, instrument metrics/alerts for throttling, add incident playbook.

maria: Thanks — I'll create an RFC doc and a small runbook from this thread. If anyone wants to take ownership of a task, reply with :hand: and tag the task.

aditya: I'll take the rewrap lambda + rate limiting work. :hand:

ops: I'll do the VPC endpoint & networking checklist.

jon: I'll draft the IAM/grant patterns and rotation policy.

maria: Great — assigning leads and making RFC. Closing thread for now. :thumbsup:
